To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

in long-term virovirologically suppressed patients, intensification with a second integrase inhibitor (raltegravir) did not result in a reduction of HIV-1 provirus levels or an increase in CD4 T-cell counts in blood or the gut mucosa.

intensification with ralegravir did not reduce the frequency of CD 4 + T cells carrying HIV proviral DNA or increase CD 4 + cell counts in long term virologically controlled individuals on standard HAAR T therapy, and that there was no difference between blood and gut proviral load.
raltegravir, a drug which blocks the HIV enzyme integrase, does not reduce the number of cells in the body carrying HIV DNA when added to standard antiretrovials.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of raltegravr intensification on HIV-1 provirus DNA in the blood of HIV-infected individuals.
the effects of HIV infection and its treatment on gut health and function.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the addition of raltegravr to a standard ART regime in patients on stable ART for at least 4 years did not result in a reduction in HIV-1 provirus levels in blood and gut CD4+ T-cells.
raltegravir, at least in this study, does not appear to have any effect on proviral DNA in blood or gut.
intensification with ralegravir did not affect proviral DNA levels in blood or gut mucosa.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of raltegravire intensification in long term virologically controlled patients on standard HAARt does not lead to further reduction in HIV proviral load in the blood or gut mucosa, or in an increase in CD4 T cells.
we did not find a significant difference between raltegravir and placebo in the decay of HIV-1 provirus in the blood and the gut mucosa.
the use of a single agent intensification strategy with raltegravr in this study population did not have an impact on the frequency of CD+4 T cells carrying HIV DNA in the gut or the blood.
The main takeaway from our work is that
intensification with raltegravir does not reduce the level of HIV provirus in the blood or gut.
intensification of standard HAART with raltegravar does not result in further reduction in the frequency of CD+ T cells carrying proviral DNA, either in the blood or in the gut.
intensification of ART with raltegravri in long-term suppressed patients did not result in any additional reduction in HIV proviral DNA levels in blood or gut.
